title: Sorting a Jigsaw by Its Edges
subtheme: Sorting a Jigsaw by Its Edges
description: Find the flat edges and corners before filling in a jigsaw.
cardDescription: Find the flat edges and corners before filling in a jigsaw.
focus: The setting is sorting a Jigsaw by Its Edges. Match each clue to a thing, action, or description in that scene.
solvingTip: Begin with a short answer you recognize. Use its crossing letters to work toward the longer scene words.
words: Type of picture puzzle assembled from interlocking pieces
One separate part of a whole
Container with a base and sides
Image made with a camera or pencil
Furniture with a flat top and legs
Hue, such as red or blue
Outline or form of an object
Find two items that go together

answerNotes.PIECE: A piece is one part of a whole. Matching shape, color, and edges helps a jigsaw piece fit its correct place.
answerNotes.CORNER: A corner is where two edges meet. In a jigsaw, a corner piece normally has two outer edges.
answerNotes.BOX: A box is a container rather than its contents. In a hobby clue, a kit may come in a box but the two words are not interchangeable.
answerNotes.TABLE: A table provides a raised flat surface. Chairs are the separate furniture used to sit beside it.
answerNotes.COLOR: Color names such as red, blue, and yellow describe appearance. They can help with a flower scene without requiring botanical vocabulary.

title: A Model Airplane on the Worktable
subtheme: A Model Airplane on the Worktable
description: Assemble and paint the small parts of a model flying machine.
cardDescription: Assemble and paint the small parts of a model flying machine.
focus: The setting is a Model Airplane on the Worktable. Match each clue to a thing, action, or description in that scene.
solvingTip: Begin with a short answer you recognize. Use its crossing letters to work toward the longer scene words.
words: Small representation of a larger object
Flying vehicle with wings and an engine
Side surface that helps an airplane fly
Rear extension of an animal's body
Colored coating spread with a brush
Rotating blades providing thrust on an early powered airplane
Set of parts for making a model
One piece of a larger whole
Round part that turns on an axle
Decorative picture transferred onto a model
Main central part of an object

answerNotes.WING: Wings help birds, many insects, and airplanes fly, but their structures differ. The model-airplane scene uses a fixed surface rather than feathers.
answerNotes.TAIL: Tail can name the rear part of an animal or a trailing end of ribbon or a kite. The word describes different things with a similar extending position.
answerNotes.GLUE: Glue bonds surfaces together as it sets. Tape holds them with an adhesive already attached to a strip.
answerNotes.PAINT: Paint leaves a colored coating on a surface. A stain usually allows more of wood's natural grain to remain visible.
answerNotes.WHEEL: A wheel rotates around an axle. Its tire is an outer covering, not another name for the entire wheel.
answerNotes.SCALE: A scale measures weight. Its reading is different from a price, although a shop may calculate price using that weight.

title: Solving a Word Search with a Pencil
subtheme: Solving a Word Search with a Pencil
description: Look for hidden words in rows, columns, and diagonals.
cardDescription: Look for hidden words in rows, columns, and diagonals.
focus: The setting is solving a Word Search with a Pencil. Match each clue to a thing, action, or description in that scene.
solvingTip: Begin with a short answer you recognize. Use its crossing letters to work toward the longer scene words.
words: Group of letters with a meaning
Pattern of crossing rows and columns
Writing tool with a graphite core
Line of things side by side
Vertical line of letters in a word grid
Line joining opposite corners of a square sheet
Material used for writing or wrapping

answerNotes.LETTER: Letter can mean a written message or one alphabet character. An envelope clue points to the message sense.
answerNotes.CIRCLE: A circle is a round line or shape. In a marble game, a drawn circle can mark the playing area.
answerNotes.PENCIL: The writing core of a modern pencil is graphite, not metallic lead. Lead remains a traditional everyday name for it.
answerNotes.ROW: A row is a line of things side by side. Garden plants, theater seats, and letters in a puzzle can all be arranged in rows.
answerNotes.LIST: A list records items in order. Checking off a purchased item is different from changing the price or quantity of it.
answerNotes.PAPER: Paper can be folded, cut, and written on. Card stock is heavier and stiffer, making it useful for tags and greeting cards.
answerNotes.LINE: Line can mean a row, a drawn mark, or a fishing cord. The clue's action helps distinguish those meanings.

title: A Game of Solitaire at the Table
subtheme: A Game of Solitaire at the Table
description: Lay out a deck for a familiar one-player card game.
cardDescription: Lay out a deck for a familiar one-player card game.
focus: The setting is a Game of Solitaire at the Table. Match each clue to a thing, action, or description in that scene.
solvingTip: Begin with a short answer you recognize. Use its crossing letters to work toward the longer scene words.
words: Card commonly marked with the letter A
Piece of stiff paper carrying a message
Face card ranked above a queen
Face card ranked between jack and king
Face card commonly marked with the letter J
Card group such as hearts or spades
Red card suit with a two-lobed symbol
Black card suit with a three-leaf symbol
Black card suit with a pointed leaf symbol
Red card suit with a four-pointed symbol

answerNotes.ACE: An ace is a playing card marked with A. Its value depends on the rules of the game being played.
answerNotes.CARD: Card can mean a printed greeting or a playing piece. An envelope points to a greeting; a deck or suit points to a game.
answerNotes.DECK: Deck can mean a pack of playing cards or an outdoor platform. Cards and a patio use different senses of the same short word.
answerNotes.KING: King can mean a ruler or a face card representing one. In a card deck, it belongs to a suit rather than ruling a country.
answerNotes.SUIT: Suit can mean matching clothes or a group of playing cards. Hearts, diamonds, clubs, and spades are the four card suits.
answerNotes.HEART: Hearts is one of the two red card suits. Its rounded symbol is different from the pointed diamond symbol in the other red suit.

subtheme: A Domino Line Along the Table
description: Match the marked ends of tiles in a growing tabletop line.
cardDescription: Match the marked ends of tiles in a growing tabletop line.
focus: The setting is a Domino Line Along the Table. Match each clue to a thing, action, or description in that scene.
solvingTip: Begin with a short answer you recognize. Use its crossing letters to work toward the longer scene words.
words: Rectangular game tile divided into two marked ends
Small flat piece used in a game or pattern
Straight mark drawn with a ruler
Domino with matching numbers at both ends
Raised surface for meals or work
Tiles held by a domino player
Informal name for a domino tile

answerNotes.DOMINO: A domino tile has two marked ends. A double has the same count on both ends.
answerNotes.DOT: Dot is the everyday word for a small round mark. On dominoes, the groups of dots indicate each end's value.
answerNotes.WHITE: White is a color description, not a flower or bird name. Crossings can help when a clue asks for a color rather than a species.
answerNotes.LINE: Line can mean a row, a drawn mark, or a fishing cord. The clue's action helps distinguish those meanings.
answerNotes.TABLE: A table provides a raised flat surface. Chairs are the separate furniture used to sit beside it.
answerNotes.HAND: Hand can name a body part or a clock pointer. A clock's minute hand makes a full turn each hour.
